title: Adaptive speculative decode: kernel fingerprinting, per-tenant acceptance tuning, and deterministic degrade path
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive speculative decoding runtime feature that reduces tail latency and cost by routing requests to fast speculative decoders when safe, while ensuring deterministic and well-instrumented fallback to conservative decoding when acceptance confidence is low. This ticket covers kernel fingerprinting for routing, a lightweight prefill probe to compute acceptance metrics, per-tenant tunables for acceptance thresholds, and a deterministic degrade path (no opaque retries).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can derive a kernel fingerprint for any model variant and expose it to the routing layer within 2ms of model load
Prefill probe: a 1-2 token probe that executes on the speculative candidate and returns an acceptance score within the runtime request window
Acceptance metrics implemented: logit-delta, topk-overlap, and normalized perplexity; thresholds can be set per-customer and per-route
Fallback path is deterministic: when probe fails acceptance or kernel mismatch occurs, request routes to the conservative decoder without speculative retries
End-to-end tests and an A/B experiment are provisioned showing >= 12% P95 latency improvement for chat-like workloads with <1.5% delta in semantic accuracy (per eval prompt set)
Observability: dashboards show acceptance_rate, probe_cost_per_request, correctness_delta, and tail latency by model and tenant
activity: 2026-03-02 - Created ticket. Initial problem statement and high-level approach added. Noted dependencies on runtime kernel registry (ENG-48001) and telemetry pipeline (ENG-49910).

2026-03-04 - Architecture sync with infra: decided to store kernel fingerprint as a compact 64-bit hash attached to model metadata. Trade-off: small storage vs need to rehash on model conversion. Action: add model fingerprint to model ingest path.

2026-03-06 - Proof-of-concept: implemented probe harness in local dev runtime. Probe runs on a lightweight quantized variant and returns top5 logits and timing. Observed median probe time 1.8ms on A100-v4.

2026-03-07 - Design review with PM & Research. Feedback: add per-tenant safety multiplier and default conservative thresholds for new tenants. Also requested explicit cost accounting for probe tokens in billing data. Added labels and telemetry hooks.

2026-03-09 - Engineering decision: acceptance metric set to combined score = weighted(logit_delta, topk_overlap, perplexity_norm). Default weights 0.6/0.3/0.1. We'll expose weights via tenant config. Rationale: logit_delta correlates best with decode divergence in evals.

2026-03-10 - Implemented deterministic fallback: runtime will mark request as 'no-speculation' and route to conservative pool. This avoids stateful speculative retries that previously caused double-billing confusion. Added unit tests for idempotent route switching.

2026-03-12 - QA run: integration test harness executed 50k chat requests in local cluster. Acceptance_rate varied by prompt distribution (35-78%). Noted high false-negative rate on long-prefix contexts -> follow-up probe improvement required (ENG-51237).
2026-03-13 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2785 (spec-probe + kernel fingerprint plumbing). Seeking review from @maria-chen and @owen-lee.

2026-03-14 - Performance note: on conversational workloads with many short requests, speculative path reduces average token cost by 9% and P95 latency by 14% in lab workload. Added acceptance tests to guard semantic accuracy regressions.
Next: finalize tenant config API, add probe sampling controls, and schedule A/B rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) after telemetry stability
notes: Avoid overfitting acceptance thresholds to synthetic QA prompts. Plan: use a small canonical evaluation set per tenant (10-20 prompts) during rollout to adjust safety multiplier. Also ensure cost metrics include probe execution tokens and add a visible warning in Console when speculative savings are below threshold.
